Introduction

Easy2edit is a simple, modular management system (CMS) for portals, websites, webshops and communities. It is built on a Django (REST) backend and a Next.js frontend, which together keep the system fast and reliable while allowing a flexible, modern way of working.

Rather than starting from a fixed template, you build a website from blocks and switch modules and plugins on or off, depending on what your site needs. This means you only use what you actually need, and you can grow your site over time by adding more functionality when required.

## What makes Easy2edit modular

The modular approach is at the heart of Easy2edit. Instead of one rigid package, the system is made up of smaller building blocks that you can combine:

- Modules are parts of the system that can be switched on or off. They are managed in Super admin > Modules.
- Plugins are signed extension packages that bring their own pages and modules. They are managed in Admin > Plugins.

This allows a site to stay lean when only basic functionality is needed, and to expand easily when new features, pages or tools are required.

## Who uses Easy2edit

There are three kinds of people who work with the system, each with a different level of access:

- Users are visitors with an account. They use the site, for example as customers, members or community participants.
- Admins manage parts of the site. Their rights come from the roles assigned to them, so one admin might manage only content, while another manages a webshop or a community area.
- Superadmins are the owner or reseller of the site. They have access to everything, including system settings, modules, plugins, prices and the licence.

This structure means that day-to-day management can be safely delegated to admins, while full control over the system stays with the superadmin.

## The dashboard

After logging in, users, admins and superadmins work from the dashboard. It is organised into three areas:

- Dashboard: your own profile, notifications and your own AI credit.
- Admin: the management area, where admins configure and maintain parts of the site.
- Super admin: the system area, reserved for superadmins, where system-wide settings, modules, plugins, prices and the licence are managed.

Which of these areas you see, and what you can do inside them, depends on whether you are a user, an admin or a superadmin.

## Standard installations

To make it easy to start a new site, Easy2edit offers standard installations. With one click, a standard installation sets the modules, plugins and theme for a particular type of website, such as a standard website, web shop, company website, business network, intranet, dating platform, sports club, foundation, marketplace or game hall.

Each installation is shown as a small tile with a settings pop-up. This pop-up is visible in the admin area and is also offered the first time an installation is set up. It lets you configure AI credit settings, modules, plugins and demo data for that type of site.

The settings pop-up has five tabs:

- General
- AI
- Modules
- Plugins
- Demo data

On the Plugins tab, a superadmin has a switch for every plugin and every module belonging to that installation. Any change made here is saved immediately as the standard for the next time this type of installation is set up, and it is written to the installations file (backend/apps/core/installations.json) that other sites receive with an update. An administrator sees the same list, but read-only, so they can check the configuration without being able to change it.

Two modules are always part of every site and cannot be switched off: Energy & emissions and Energy: collector module. These are core modules.

## The header

At the top of the screen, the header gives quick access to a few general controls:

- The language switcher, to change the display language.
- The edit-mode switch (pencil icon), to turn editing of the page on or off.
- Light/dark mode, to switch the visual theme.
- The user menu, for account-related actions.

## Getting help

Help is always close at hand. On every page of the Admin and Super admin areas, a Help button (a question mark icon, next to the back button) opens this manual in a pop-up, directly at the chapter that belongs to the page you are viewing.

On the Admin start page, under About Easy2edit, you will find two large buttons that give access to the full manual: one opens the HTML manual, either in a pop-up or in a new tab, and the other offers a PDF download. The manual itself is written in English.
Getting started

## Logging in for the first time

The first time you open Easy2edit, log in using the superadmin account. This account has full access to every module and setting, so you can complete the initial setup.

## The sandbox question (localhost only)

If the site is running on your own computer (localhost), the very first thing Easy2edit asks is whether you want to switch the sandbox on. With the sandbox switched on, payments, e-mail, sms and tests of API links are only simulated: nothing real is sent or charged, even if you have entered live keys. This makes it safe to explore the system without any risk.

Your answer is remembered, so you will not be asked again. If you ever want to change this setting later, go to Admin > Sandbox.

## Standard installation

If nothing has been installed yet, a pop-up appears offering a standard installation. It has two tabs:

- Installation: choose and apply a ready-made standard installation for your type of website.
- Filling with AI: explains that the website can be filled using AI, for example by importing an existing website, translating content, or improving it with an instruction. This tab also shows whether an AI link (API key) is already available.

Take your time to read both tabs before deciding how you want to start.

## Filling the site with AI

Once a standard installation has been set, Easy2edit asks whether you want to use AI to help fill the site. If you choose yes, you are taken straight to buying AI credit.

A welcome pop-up then explains how AI credit works and allows the superadmin to put the credit settings in place. Details on how AI credit, tokens and costs work are explained in the AI chapter of this manual.

## Setting up the basics

Once the initial pop-ups are done, take the following steps to get your website ready:

1. Go to Admin > System to set the basics: site name, company data, contact data and addresses.
2. Choose a standard installation if you have not done so yet, either from the Super admin overview or at Admin > Standard installations.
3. Go to Admin > Theme and Admin > Logos & images to choose a theme and upload your logos.
4. Go to Admin > Languages to choose which languages your website will use.
5. Go to Admin > Users and Roles to create the user accounts and roles your team needs.

These five steps give your website its identity, its look, its language settings and its first users, and form the foundation for everything else you do in Easy2edit.

## Getting to know the modules

Easy2edit is built from modules, each handling one part of the website: pages and menus, the media library, the webshop and payments, chat and messaging, profiles, security, AI, and many more. Every module can be switched on or off, and most have their own settings page under Admin.

A full overview of all available modules, with the option to switch them on or off, can be found at Admin > Modulebeheer (Module management). This page is only visible to superadmins.

Some modules are especially relevant while you are getting started:

- Pagina's en menu (pages): manage your pages, the header menu and your own links.
- Bewerkmodus (edit_mode): edit texts, formatting and images directly on the website using a switch in the header.
- Mediabibliotheek (media): manage all images and videos, stored locally or on S3.
- Site importeren (siteimport): import an existing website (address, folder or ZIP), including its theme, pages, homepage, icons and images.
- Plugins (plugins): upload separate programs that work together with the system; available only to superadmins, since plugins run as trusted code.
- Sandbox (sandbox): the test environment described above, used to simulate e-mail, sms, payments and other external services.
- AI (ai): covers all AI usage in the system, including who asks what, how many tokens are used and what it costs. This module is automatically active as soon as an AI link (API key) exists, and the superadmin sees its dashboard.

You do not need to configure every module right away. Start with the basic setup described above, then explore Admin > Modulebeheer to switch on the modules your website needs, such as a webshop, subscriptions, chat, or SEO tools. Each module is explained in more detail later in this manual.
Pages, menu and edit mode

This chapter explains how pages and the menu are organised in Easy2edit, and how edit mode lets you build and change pages directly on the screen.

## Pages and menu overview

All pages and menu items are managed under Admin > Pages. You will find three kinds of entries here:

- System pages: built-in pages such as Home and products.
- Own pages: text pages that live at an address such as /p/<key>.
- Links and menu items: entries that point elsewhere or structure the menu itself.

## Page settings

Each page has its own set of settings that control how it looks, who can see it and how it behaves in the menu.

- Names per language: you can set a different name for each language, and use AI translation to fill in the other languages automatically.
- Address per language: the web address of the page can also differ per language.
- Visibility: choose who may see the page - everybody, logged-in users, guests only, or specific users or groups.
- Menu visibility: decide whether the page should show in the header menu.
- Open in new tab: choose whether clicking the page opens it in the same tab or a new one.
- Devices: control whether the page is shown on desktop, tablet, mobile, or a combination.
- Page-specific theme/header/footer: a page can use its own theme, header or footer instead of the site-wide default.
- SEO per language: set SEO details separately for each language.
- Background: add a background image or video to the page.

## Switching on edit mode

To start editing a page directly on the screen, switch on the pencil icon in the header. This activates edit mode, which overlays editing tools on top of the live page.

## How pages are built: rows, cells and items

In edit mode, pages are constructed from rows, which act as horizontal blocks stacked on the page.

- Each row can be divided into cells, from 1 up to 4 columns wide.
- Each cell holds one or more items, placed through + Add.

Available items include:

- Heading
- Text (rich text editing)
- Image
- Button
- Spacer
- Line
- System objects
- Ready-made parts: contact data, social media, map, video, quote, figures, logo, opening hours
- HTML / CSS code

## Row settings

Click the gear icon in the corner of a row to open its settings. From here you can control:

- Background colour, image or video
- Overlay
- Padding
- Width: column, wide or full screen
- Hero height
- Text colour
- Rounded corners
- Space above the row

## Cell settings

Each cell within a row has its own settings:

- Width
- Alignment
- Card style: background, border, radius and shadow

## Text and button settings

Text items can be styled individually:

- Style, size, colour and font
- Padding
- Background, shown as a label or pill

Buttons have their own set of options:

- Label per language
- Link
- Style: primary, outline or ghost
- Colours
- Size
- Icon

## The HTML / CSS code part

For advanced customisation, the HTML / CSS code item opens a large pop-up with three tabs: Visual, HTML and CSS.

- In the Visual tab, you click directly into the text and type, seeing the result exactly as it will appear (what you see is what you get). A toolbar offers bold, italic, underline, list, link and clear formatting, plus a switch between a light and dark background for the editing area.
- The HTML tab lets you edit the underlying markup directly.
- The CSS tab lets you add custom styling.

The code you add runs inside a sandboxed frame, meaning it has no rights on the rest of the site. This keeps your pages safe even when custom code is used.

## System objects

System objects are modular pieces such as donation buttons, subscriptions, media views, plugin parts and, for superadmins, AI dashboard blocks. Before they can be used, the relevant module must be switched on in Admin > System objects.

Once enabled, you can place a system object into a page while in edit mode via + Add > System objects.

## Editing pages imported from HTML

Pages that were taken over 1 to 1 from an HTML file, as described in the Site import process, behave slightly differently in edit mode. Every text and button on such a page shows a pencil icon.

1. Click the pencil on the text or button you want to change.
2. An editor opens showing the text as it appears on the page, with formatting options for bold, italic, underline and link. For buttons, you can also edit the link.
3. Click Save to write your changes back into the page.

This approach lets you safely update imported HTML pages without needing to edit the underlying code directly.
Importing a website (Site import)

Easy2edit can turn an existing website into a working Easy2edit site. You give it one or more HTML files, an address, a folder or a ZIP file, and the built-in AI reads it and prepares a proposal. Nothing is created on your site until you look at the proposal and approve it.

You find this feature under Admin > Imported. The button is called 'Site import' the first time you use it. Once a site has been imported, the same button is labelled 'Imported'.

## What the AI proposes

After reading the file or files, the AI puts together a proposal that includes:

- A theme: colours, fonts, corner roundings and content width.
- The pages found in the file.
- The content of those pages.
- Icons and images, which are placed in the media library tagged 'import'.
- The modules needed to support the content, for example the FAQ module when the source site has a list of questions and answers.

You review this proposal before anything is built. Nothing is installed or created on your website until you approve.

## Building a design with the AI creator

Go to Admin > Imported > tab AI creator and choose New design to start a wizard. The wizard has seven steps: Start, Style, Colours, Pages, Modules, Photos and Preview. Everything you type is saved automatically as a concept. If you close the window while a design is still a concept, you are asked whether to save it (it stays under My designs), delete it, or carry on working.

The Start step contains a block called 'Quick start with an external AI'. It explains three steps:

1. Choose the modules and plugins you want.
2. Copy the prompt and paste it into an external AI such as Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini.
3. Read the resulting ZIP file back into Easy2edit.

The button 'Copy AI prompt' builds a prompt from all your choices and copies it to the clipboard. The button 'Modules and plugins (n/m)' lets you switch each module and plugin on or off. Modules and plugins that belong to your active standard installation are on by default. If you switch on something that is not part of your standard installation, a warning tells you that your monthly price goes up, and by how much, excluding VAT; the total monthly price of your installation plus the extras you picked is shown under the list. Only what is switched on is used in the prompt, by the external AI, and later during the import.

The prompt itself contains the design guidelines of the page editor (bands, hero, cells, cards, blocks), the rules the ZIP file must follow, and, for every extra language your website uses, the format of a translation file.

## The ZIP file

Whether it comes from the quick-start prompt or is built another way, the ZIP file read by Easy2edit (tab ZIP file, or 'Read ZIP file' in the wizard) must follow these rules:

- At most 12 HTML pages. Every html file becomes a page, including pages that are only linked from the footer.
- One style.css file.
- A folder img/ with at most 40 pictures (jpg, png, webp or svg), each at most 5 MB. File names use only lowercase letters, digits, - and _, and are at most 40 characters long.
- Everything sits in the top folder of the ZIP; other folders are skipped, and the import notes mention what was skipped.
- Backgrounds set through CSS, including through CSS variables, are picked up. SVG files are cleaned.
- A file name that breaks the naming rule is renamed automatically, and every reference to it in the HTML and CSS is rewritten to match.

For each extra language, the ZIP can include a file named vertalingen-<code>.json, in the format easy2edit-vertalingen/1. It states the source language, the target language, and per page a list of items with the element, the source text and its translation. When the site is translated, texts from this file are used first; only missing texts are translated by the AI. The import notes report how many texts came from the file and how many from the AI.

## Applying the import

Once you approve the proposal, the theme is installed and put to use. Then the Apply panel opens, with tabs Pages, Links, Buttons, Header, Footer and Theme.

Pages: drag and drop between two columns, pages from the file on the left and pages of your website on the right, to link a file page to an existing page (for example Home) or keep it as its own new page. For each page choose the view:

- Exact: the page looks exactly like the HTML file. Texts and buttons can still be edited with the pencil in edit mode.
- Editable: the AI rebuilds the page using page builder blocks. Cards, label pills, band colours, rows and hero sections are rebuilt. Anything the blocks cannot reproduce, such as a progress bar, a checklist or preview cards, becomes an 'HTML / CSS code' block.

You can give the AI an optional instruction, for example 'make the headings bigger'. You also choose what happens to content already on the page: clear it first, replace only the blocks from this import, or add the new content below the existing content, and whether the pages should also be translated into your other languages.

Links and Buttons: link the links and buttons found in the file to pages or parts of your website by drag and drop.

Header: switch the system header to the header from the file, giving you the bigger menu with the file's links and buttons.

Footer: show the system footer underneath the imported pages.

Theme: adjust colours, default mode, content width and roundings.

## Progress, status and re-applying

While the import runs, a pop-up shows progress as a percentage. When it finishes, a 'Go to page' button appears. The original HTML is kept, so you can apply the import again later with a new instruction. Each import shows a status, either Pending or Active.

The list of pages belonging to an import shows, per page: name, whether it is in the menu, whether it is visible, and its view (Exact or Editable). In Pages > page settings, an imported page has an extra tab called Import, with a field for an instruction to the AI and a button to rebuild just that one page from the original file.

## Removing an import

Removing an import puts back the theme and the content that was previously on the pages, or advises you to reinstall via the superadmin if that is not possible, and removes everything the import created.

Note that the standard home page (logo, title, text, photos) is always empty by default, so an import always overwrites it and it never shows behind an imported page.
Media, theme, languages and branding

## Media library

The media library (Admin > Media) is where you manage all the images and videos used on your website. Files can be stored locally on your server or on S3, depending on how your site is configured.

Every picture or video you upload can be given tags, which makes it easier to search and organise your files as your library grows. Once uploaded, pictures can be chosen from the media library in every pop-up across Easy2edit, so you only need to upload an image once and can then reuse it wherever you need it.

Typical uses for the media library include:

- Uploading product photos, banners or background images
- Managing video files for use on pages
- Tagging files by topic, campaign or page so they are easy to find later
- Reusing existing images instead of uploading duplicates

## Logos and branding images

The Logos & images section (branding) is where you manage the visual identity of your website. Here you can set:

- The logo, including separate versions for light and dark mode
- The favicon, which appears in browser tabs
- The app icon, used if your website is saved as an app on a device
- The photos shown on the homepage

Keeping these elements up to date ensures your website looks consistent and professional across devices and browsers.

## Theme and design

The Vormgeving (theme) section, found at Admin > Theme, controls the overall look and feel of your website. When switched off, the website uses the standard style. When switched on, you gain access to a wide range of design options.

With the theme settings you can adjust:

- Colours for both light mode and dark mode
- Fonts used throughout the website
- Roundings, such as the corners of buttons and boxes
- Content width, controlling how wide the main content area appears
- Header layout, including an editorial layout with a side menu
- Pop-up style, determining how pop-up windows are displayed

Easy2edit also offers theme packs, which are ready-made combinations of these settings. You can switch between theme packs with a single click, making it easy to try different looks or quickly apply a new style across the whole site.

If you have created a design you want to reuse, or want to move a theme to another website, you can export your theme settings. Themes can also be imported, which is useful for applying a saved design or sharing a theme between projects.

Steps to apply a theme pack:

1. Go to Admin > Theme.
2. Make sure the theme section is switched on, since switching it off reverts to the standard style.
3. Browse the available theme packs.
4. Select the one you want to apply.
5. Check your website to confirm the new look is applied as expected.

## Languages

The Talen (languages) section manages multilingual support for your website. When this feature is switched off, the website only uses the default language. When switched on, you can offer your website in multiple languages.

In this section you can:

- Choose which languages your website offers to visitors
- Set the default language for the site
- Translate texts using the built-in AI translation tool

This makes it possible to reach a wider audience without manually rewriting every page in a different language.

It is worth noting that the texts of the Easy2edit system itself, such as labels and interface elements, are already available in 44 languages. This means the admin interface and built-in system texts can adapt to many languages independently of the content translations you manage yourself.

Steps to enable multiple languages:

1. Go to Admin > Languages.
2. Switch on multilingual support.
3. Select the languages you want to offer on your website.
4. Set your preferred default language.
5. Use the AI translation tool to translate your content into the selected languages.
6. Review the translated texts to make sure they read naturally before publishing.

## Bringing it all together

Media, branding, theme and language settings work together to shape how your website looks and feels to visitors. The media library keeps your images and videos organised and ready to use. The branding settings ensure your logo and icons are consistent everywhere they appear. The theme settings let you fine-tune or completely transform the design, with theme packs offering quick, ready-made styles. Finally, the language settings allow your website to speak to visitors in the language they prefer, while the system interface itself can already be used in 44 languages.

Taking time to set these up carefully, even before focusing on individual pages, will give your website a strong, professional and accessible foundation.
Users, roles and security

## Users and profiles

Easy2edit keeps a record of everyone who can log in to your website or admin area. You manage these records under Admin > Users (users).

For each user you can set up:

- An account with a username and password
- A profile photo
- A public profile that can be shown on the website
- A blocked or active status

Blocking an account is useful when someone leaves the organisation or should temporarily lose access, without deleting their history or content. You can remove accounts completely when they are no longer needed.

## Dashboard and personal profile

Every user who logs in lands on the dashboard & profiel (dashboard) area. From here people can:

- Log in and reach their personal dashboard
- View and update their own profile
- See the information that is relevant to their role

This is the starting point for anyone working in the admin area, from a single editor to a full administrator.

## User groups

Where users are individual accounts, user groups let you organise people together. A group can be given one or more roles and access to specific modules, so you do not have to configure every person one by one.

Typical use of groups:

1. Create a group for a team or department
2. Assign the roles that team should have
3. Give the group access to the modules it needs
4. Add the relevant users to the group

Any user added to a group inherits the rights and module access of that group.

## Roles and rights

Roles (roles) determine what a user or group is allowed to see and do in the admin area. A role is a set of rights, for example:

- Content manager
- Moderator
- View AI use of users

Each right opens a specific part of the admin area. By combining rights into roles, you can give people exactly the access they need, no more and no less.

Superadmins always have every right, regardless of role settings. This ensures there is always at least one account that can fully manage the website, even if role configuration is incomplete.

If the Rollen module is switched off, only superadmins have rights in the system. This is a safe fallback, but it means other users will not be able to work in the admin area until roles are configured.

## Module access per user or group

Besides roles, access to individual modules can also be granted directly to a specific user or group. This is managed under Super admin > Modules, using the person icon next to a module.

This gives you two complementary ways to control access:

- Roles control which rights a user or group has across the admin area
- Direct module access controls whether a particular user or group can use a specific module

Use roles for broad, reusable sets of permissions, and per-user or per-group module access for exceptions or very specific needs.

## General security settings

The algemene beveiliging (security_basic) module covers the core security settings for the admin area, including:

- Inlogslot (login lock), which protects against repeated failed login attempts
- Session duration, controlling how long a user stays logged in
- Password rules, so accounts meet a minimum strength
- Security headers, which add technical protection to how the website responds to requests

Review these settings regularly, especially after adding new administrators or changing your security requirements.

Two-step verification is also available as part of the security options, adding a second check beyond the password when users log in.

## Visitor-facing protection

Several modules protect your visitors or control who can reach your website at all:

- Landcontrole (geo): blocks or allows access to the website per country, based on IP address
- Leeftijdscontrole (age_gate): shows an 18+ popup to visitors before they can continue
- Gokken-popup (gambling): shows a combined age and warning popup, intended for gambling-related content
- Cookies (cookies): manages the cookie banner, visitor preferences and the cookie policy popup
- Woordfilter (word_filter): blocks forbidden words in texts, names and captions submitted on the website

These modules are configured independently and can be combined as needed, for example using both the country control and the age check on the same website.

## Practical recommendations

- Keep the number of superadmin accounts small, since they always have full access
- Use roles and groups rather than configuring every user individually
- Review blocked and unused accounts periodically and remove or deactivate them
- Enable login lock, session limits and password rules as a minimum baseline
- Turn on two-step verification for administrator accounts where possible
- If your website targets specific regions or has legal age requirements, configure Landcontrole, Leeftijdscontrole or the Gokken-popup accordingly
- Set up the cookie banner and policy before publishing a public website, to meet visitor consent requirements
Shop, orders, payments, subscriptions and donations

Chapter 7: Shop, orders, payments, subscriptions and donations

Easy2edit offers a set of plugins that work together to sell products, manage orders, process payments and run subscriptions or donation campaigns. Depending on what you want to offer on your site, you combine the Webshop, Orders, Financieel and Abonnementen plugins. Understanding how these plugins depend on each other will help you set everything up correctly.

## How the plugins work together

- Webshop needs the Orders and Betalen (Payments) plugins to function.
- Orders can work on its own, for example if you only want to let customers pay by invoice. The Betalen and Webshop plugins both need Orders to work.
- Financieel brings together everything related to money: payment methods, VAT rates, shipping options and the layout of financial documents. Orders, Webshop and Abonnementen all need this plugin.
- Abonnementen needs the Orders plugin, since every subscription period or donation generates an order.

In short, Orders is the central plugin for anything that results in a transaction, Financieel handles the money side, and Webshop and Abonnementen are the two ways customers can place an order.

## Webshop

The Webshop plugin lets you sell products online. You manage:

- Products and product groups
- Variants, such as colour or size, each with their own price
- Staggered pricing (staffelprijzen), where the price changes depending on the quantity ordered
- Shipping methods and discount codes

Easy2edit includes demo content with ready-made shop pages: a products page, a shopping cart page and a checkout page. You can use these as a starting point and adjust them to fit your site.

To set up a basic webshop:

1. Go to Admin > Plugins and activate Webshop, Orders and Betalen.
2. Add your products and organise them into product groups.
3. Create any variants your products need, such as size or colour, and set a price for each variant.
4. Set up staggered pricing if you want to offer quantity discounts.
5. Configure your shipping methods and, optionally, discount codes.
6. Check the demo shop pages (products, shopping cart, checkout) and adjust them to match your site.

## Orders

The Orders plugin manages orders for the entire site, not just the webshop. It handles orders coming from the webshop, from subscriptions and from donations in one place. Here you manage:

- Order status, so you can follow an order from placement to completion
- VAT settings
- The confirmation email sent to customers after an order is placed

Orders can also work independently of the Webshop plugin. This is useful if you only want to accept orders paid by invoice, without running a full online shop.

## Financieel

The Financieel plugin is where all money-related settings come together:

- Payment methods and payment terms
- The connections to the payment providers Stripe and Mollie
- VAT rates, with a standard high and low rate that you link to your products
- Shipping options
- The layout of invoices, quotes, packing slips and return slips

Since Orders, Webshop and Abonnementen all depend on Financieel, this plugin forms the financial backbone of any paid feature on your site.

## Abonnementen (Subscriptions and donations)

The Abonnementen plugin lets you offer subscription plans and donation campaigns.

Subscriptions give visitors access to parts of your site, such as pages, content, chat, video, likes or services. A subscription can be:

- A one-time purchase
- A recurring subscription, with a new order generated for each period

Donation campaigns let visitors choose an amount to give using a slider, moving between a minimum and a maximum value you set.

Actions determine what is free and what requires payment, so you can combine free and paid content on the same site using subscription plans.

To set up a subscription or donation:

1. Activate the Abonnementen plugin, which requires Orders to be active.
2. Create a subscription plan and decide whether it is a one-time purchase or a recurring subscription.
3. Link the plan to the pages, content, chat, video, likes or services it should unlock.
4. For donations, set up a donation action and define the minimum and maximum amount for the slider.
5. Use actions to decide which parts of your site remain free and which require a subscription or donation.

## Payments and the sandbox

Payments made through the Webshop, Orders or Abonnementen plugins are processed through Stripe or Mollie, both configured in the Financieel plugin. Before going live, you can use the sandbox to simulate payments. This lets you test the full order and payment flow, from checkout to confirmation, without processing any real transactions.
Community, marketplace, agenda, documents and games

This chapter covers the plugins that bring your members together: profiles, dating-style discovery, messaging, chat, direct connections, a marketplace, an agenda, document management, a games hall, showcase presentations, and the related age, country and gambling checks.

## Community

The Community plugin brings together everything you need for a community or dating site: profile pages with photos, a member search, blocking unwanted users, searching and matching (liking, favorites, visitors), private messages, chat, and a direct connection via WebRTC using a code, link or QR code.

Community works with profile themes, profile fields and "available for" options, so you can tailor the profile experience to your audience. When parts of the community should require a subscription or a donation, Community works together with the Subscriptions plugin.

## Profile themes

Profile themes define how member profiles look and which fields they have. Easy2edit comes with ready-made theme packages: Sporters, Dating, Business and Webshop. You can install or remove these packages, or build your own theme with its own fields, visibility settings and search filters.

The superadmin decides which themes administrators and users are allowed to choose. Themes can be exported and imported as JSON, which makes it easy to reuse or share a theme between sites.

## Community building blocks

- Profiles (profiles): a personal profile page with multiple photos, visibility per language and group, a member search, and the ability to block other users.
- Discover (discover): search and meet other users as on a dating site, with filters, recommendations, liking, matches, favorites and visitors.
- Messages (messages): a messaging system between users, with its own inbox.
- Chat (chat): chat in a popup or full screen, either through the portal or directly via WebRTC, including photos, video and video chat.
- Direct connection (directconnect): a direct WebRTC connection between two people using a code, link or QR code, even without an account. It supports chat, photos, video and video chat, and is available on the pages /directconnect and /direct.

## Marketplace

The marketplace lets members offer products, services or anything else for sale, each with a theme and images. An item can have:

- a fixed price
- bidding, starting from a minimum price
- a booking, for example an appointment or signing up for an event

Bids are visible to all members, so everyone can follow how an item is doing.

## Agenda

The agenda gives users and groups a shared calendar. It supports:

- personal appointments
- appointments with other members, including invitations, confirmations or proposing another time
- group appointments
- events created by administrators, which can be placed on pages as a system object

The agenda includes reminders, notifications and a tile on the dashboard, so members are kept up to date on what is coming up.

## Document management

Document management lets you upload files into a folder structure, with tags, versions and rights per user or group. Files can be stored on the server or on S3, and can be encrypted for extra protection.

Blocks are available to show documents directly on pages, so you can present shared files, manuals or member documents wherever needed.

## Games

The games hall offers a space for your members to play. Each game is its own package, delivered as a folder or zip containing a game.json file, placed in the games folder of this plugin. A game has its own configuration for management and its own settings per member.

Games run in a sandboxed environment and keep track of scores and progress. The games hall supports ranglijsten (leaderboards) and comes with an example game to show how it works.

## Age, country and gambling checks

For sites that need it, Easy2edit offers an age check (18+), a country check, and a gambling popup (24+). These are only meant for target groups where such checks are required or desired.

The settings for these checks are found under Beveiliging (Security). The popups and the country check only work when this plugin is switched on.

## Showcase

Showcase lets you present your projects to visitors. Each project can include a title, a short text, a description, a goal, a link, a duration and a budget, together with pictures and videos (YouTube, Vimeo or an mp4/webm link). Every one of these fields can be switched on or off in the plugin settings, shown as columns of switches.

Projects also have a status (active, in development, offline), shared tags for searching, and groups that can have subgroups; choosing a group automatically includes its subgroups.

The admin page is organized in four tabs:

- Projects
- Groups
- Tags
- Presentations

A project itself is edited in a popup with the tabs General, Content, Media and Translations.

A presentation decides how a selection of projects is displayed: as a grid, list, table, photo wall (masonry), scroller or slider. A project can open on its own page (/showcase/<name>), in a popup, or in place on the same page. Presentations can include a search field and filters on tags, groups and status, and can be limited to certain fields, a specific group, specific tags, a specific status, or only featured projects.

Every active presentation is a system object, so you can place it on a page in edit mode. Three standard presentations always exist: search, scroller and list.

Public pages are available at /showcase and /showcase/<name>.

To help you explore Showcase quickly, demo content is available: 9 projects, groups, tags and 6 presentations. You can add or remove this demo content with a single button on the plugin page.
SEO, FAQ and statistics

## SEO

Easy2edit helps you make your website easy to find, not only for traditional search engines but also for bots and AI agents that read and summarise web content. The SEO tools in Easy2edit take care of the technical basics as well as the content details that search engines and AI systems look for.

Out of the box, Easy2edit takes care of:

- robots.txt, which tells search engines and other bots which parts of your site they may or may not visit.
- A sitemap, an overview of all your pages that helps search engines find and index your content efficiently.
- llms.txt, a file aimed at AI agents and language models, describing your site in a way that helps them understand and reference it correctly.
- Page titles and descriptions, the short pieces of text that appear in search results and that explain what a page is about.
- Structured data, extra information added to your pages that helps search engines and AI agents understand the meaning of your content, such as what is a product, an article, a question, or an event.

As a website owner, you generally do not need to build these elements yourself. Easy2edit generates and maintains them automatically based on the content of your pages, modules and plugins. This means that as you add or update pages, your SEO information stays up to date without extra manual work.

## FAQ

The FAQ module lets you publish your own frequently asked questions and answers on your website, on the page /faq.

Key points about the FAQ module:

- You create and manage your own questions and answers, tailored to your organisation and your visitors.
- Questions and answers can be translated, so visitors can read your FAQ in their own language.
- If your website was imported from an existing site that already had frequently asked questions, those questions are automatically placed into this FAQ module, so you do not have to recreate them by hand.
- The FAQ content lives on the /faq page.

To make sure visitors can actually find your FAQ, add the page to your site menu:

1. Go to Admin > Pages.
2. Locate the FAQ page, or create it if it does not yet exist.
3. Add the page to the relevant menu so it appears in your site navigation.

Because the FAQ page is a normal page within Pages, you manage its placement in the menu the same way as any other page on your site.

## Statistics

The Statistics area gives you a clear overview of what is happening on your website, combining graphs and figures from across your entire site in one place.

The statistics overview includes information such as:

- Visitors, so you can see how many people are visiting your site and how that develops over time.
- SEO, giving insight into how your site is performing in terms of search engine visibility.
- Bots, showing activity from automated crawlers visiting your website.
- AI calls, showing how often AI agents or language models access your content.

In addition to these overall figures, Statistics also brings together data from the rest of your website:

- Every module and every plugin that collects data gets its own section, or tab, within Statistics.
- Modules and plugins send their figures directly to this central statistics area, so you do not need to check many different places to understand how your site is doing.
- The statistics are presented using widgets with charts, making trends and patterns easy to read at a glance.

One important thing to keep in mind is that statistics depend on the module or plugin being active:

- If a particular plugin is switched off, it will not collect or send any data to Statistics.
- This means that no figures will be counted or shown for that plugin while it is disabled.
- If you want to track a certain type of activity, make sure the related module or plugin is enabled.

Together, SEO, FAQ and Statistics help you present your website clearly to visitors, search engines and AI agents, while also giving you the insight you need to understand how your site is actually being used.
AI and AI credit

Easy2edit uses artificial intelligence (Claude, by Anthropic) throughout the system to help with tasks such as translating content, writing page texts, importing websites, researching prices and more. Every single call made to the AI is logged in detail, so that usage and costs stay fully transparent and controllable.

## What gets monitored

For every AI call, the system records:

- Who made the request (a user, an admin, a superadmin, or the system itself)
- From which part of the system the call came
- Which AI model was used
- The number of tokens sent and received
- How long the call took
- Whether it succeeded
- What it cost

This information feeds the AI dashboard, which gives superadmins full insight into usage patterns and spending.

## The AI module and AI links

The AI module is a core module. It switches on automatically as soon as an AI link (an API key) is installed and enabled under Admin > API keys.

A link can be marked as a Superadmin link. When this is done, only superadmins can see or change it. This is used, for example, for the Easy2edit AI link and the Stripe link of the reseller.

AI calls made by users and admins always run on an Easy2edit link belonging to the superadmin, whenever one is available.

## The Super admin AI dashboard

Super admin > AI gives superadmins a full dashboard with the following tabs:

- Overview: key figures, cost over time per group, share of cost per group, and the last calls made
- Where: where AI is used most, what costs most, which tasks and models are involved, and busy hours and weekdays
- Users: heavy users, highest costs, and a table per user with a PDF button on each row
- Costs: costs broken down per month or week, per group and per user
- Credit: management of AI credit
- Blocks: dashboard blocks that can be placed on pages
- Settings: pricing, margins and related configuration

The dashboard can be filtered by period, by month (the current month plus the previous twelve), and by group. The PDF button produces a summary report, or, when 'Detailed' is selected, a complete list of every call including tokens in and out, duration and costs.

## Costs, prices and margins

Superadmins manage purchase prices per million tokens for each model, organised in tabs for Claude, OpenAI and Gemini, showing only the models currently active in the API. The 'Refresh models' button also looks up current prices directly from the AI provider.

Purchase prices are set in the purchase currency (for example USD), while sale prices are set in the selling currency (for example EUR), using an exchange rate that can be updated with a button that consults the AI.

Three separate margins can be set, each expressed as a percentage, and each split into tokens in and tokens out:

- Users
- Admins
- Reseller/superadmin

A switch determines whether usage by superadmins and the system is also charged to the customer. When switched on, this usage is booked to a group named after the website, using the reseller margin. When switched off, it is treated as a cost to the reseller with no margin applied, and shown separately.

Prices, exchange rate and margins are stored with each individual call, so later changes to settings only affect new calls, never past ones.

Only superadmins can change these system-wide AI settings.

## AI credit

By default, users and admins must purchase AI credit before they can use AI features. This requirement is a switch that is on by default. Superadmins and the system itself never need credit.

Before every AI call, the system estimates its cost and checks it against the available credit. If there is not enough credit, nothing is sent, and a message explains what is needed.

After the call completes, the actual cost is deducted from the credit balance.

When a user's credit runs low, a pop-up appears with a slider. The minimum step is based on actual use over the last 30 days (25, 50 or 100), along with a suggested amount.

Payment always goes through Stripe, using an Easy2edit link belonging to the superadmin. The website's own Stripe shop is never used for this. Credit is added once payment is confirmed, which happens when the customer returns from the payment page and again when the AI screen is opened.

Superadmins set the available top-up amounts and can manually add or deduct credit for any user, via Super admin > AI > Credit.

Every admin sees a welcome pop-up at their first login, explaining how AI and AI credit work.

On a computer where the sandbox mode is switched on, AI credit is never paid for with a real payment. Instead, a simulated payment page is used.

Each standard installation has an AI tab showing:

- Whether AI is available for this installation
- Whether credit is required
- The smallest and largest top-up amounts allowed

## What admins can see and manage

Admin > AI shows usage by users and admins for that installation. It does not show purchase prices, margins, or reseller costs. The Admin start page also includes an 'AI use' block showing the admin's own credit balance.

This area includes a table per user and a PDF report per user, without purchase prices.

To see this information, an admin needs the right 'View AI use of users', assigned via Roles.

## Admins with their own AI and Stripe links

An admin who has configured their own AI link (Anthropic) and their own Stripe link, neither marked as a superadmin link, can switch on their own credit system for their users via Admin > AI > Credit for users.

In that case:

- Their users use the admin's own AI link
- Payments go through the admin's own Stripe account
- The margin belongs to the admin

The admin sets the credit rules, the top-up amounts, and the margin, and can add credit to individual users as needed.

## AI blocks on pages

Several parts of the AI dashboard can be turned into reusable blocks: key figures, cost over time, usage per group, where AI is used, heavy users, highest costs, models, and busy hours.

These blocks are switched on as system objects via Super admin > AI > Blocks, and can then be placed on any page while in edit mode. Only superadmins can see the figures shown in these blocks.
Plugins, backups, licence and deployment

This chapter explains how to manage plugins, protect your website with backups, understand how the licence and pricing work, and how Easy2edit is deployed and kept up to date.

## Plugins

Plugins extend Easy2edit with extra modules, pages, admin screens and translations. You manage them in Admin > Plugins.

Plugins are signed packages that live in the /plugins folder. You can install new plugins from the library (resource/plugins), switch them on or off, and update them when a new version is available.

A plugin can bring its own:

- Pages
- Modules
- Translations, available in up to 44 languages
- Admin screens for configuration

Some plugins come with demo content to help you see how the plugin works. If a plugin has demo content, its page in Admin > Plugins (tab Overview) shows a button 'Make demo content'. Click it to add sample pages, texts or settings for that plugin. Once the demo content exists, the same button changes to 'Remove demo content', letting you take it away again.

Demo content is also cleaned up automatically: resetting the system removes any demo content along with it.

Two plugin related items work slightly differently:

- The module API keys is always switched on in every standard installation.
- The superadmin links (AI, Stripe, mail, storage) are switched on automatically whenever an installation is set up, so these integrations keep working. The secret keys themselves are never stored in the installations file, and any link marked Superadmin link can only be seen and changed by superadmins.

## Resetting the system

Super admin > System > Reset lets you reset the system. When you do, you are asked whether the AI data in the database should be removed as well. This includes:

- All AI calls with their costs
- The credit history and credit of superadmins

The AI settings themselves are kept. Note that the credit of normal users disappears automatically whenever those users are removed, regardless of this choice.

## Backups

Admin > Backups keeps your website safe by creating regular backups, taken per day, week or month. A backup includes:

- Pages
- Menus
- Texts
- Images
- Theme
- Settings of modules and plugins

From this screen you can restore a backup to bring the site back to an earlier state, or download a backup for safekeeping outside Easy2edit.

The standard installations basis (installations.json) is part of the system itself and is not something you need to back up separately. As with the installations file elsewhere, secret keys are never stored in it.

## Site import

If you need to bring in content from another website, use the site import feature. You can import from an address, a folder, a ZIP file or a single HTML file, and Easy2edit will read in the theme, pages, homepage, icons and images.

When you import a single HTML file, Claude creates the theme, pages and content for you, and switches on whichever modules are needed to support that content.

An imported site can be removed again at any time, together with everything that came with it.

## Licence

Admin > Licence shows the costs and payment method for your licence, which can be settled through Stripe or by invoice. The price of your licence is based on which modules and plugins you currently have switched on.

Super admin > Prices manages the pricing side for the whole platform:

- The price list, shown per month, quarter and year
- Quotations, exportable as PDF
- Marketing tiles for presenting pricing to customers
- Sales calculation tools

## Deployment

Easy2edit is deployed using Docker, with separate compose files for development and production environments. A reverse proxy handles incoming traffic and manages certificates for secure connections.

When the backend starts, it automatically runs any pending database migrations, so your installation is always kept in sync with the current version.

Every installation displays its version in the format 'Easy2edit version 1.0.0 build X'. This version number comes from one central place in the system, backend/BUILD, so you can always confirm exactly which build is running.

## Statistics for plugins

Finally, it is worth knowing how plugins relate to the Statistics area. Each module and plugin writes its own figures to its own tab within Statistics, covering visitors, SEO, bots and AI calls. If a plugin is switched off, it simply does not count anything, so no data for that plugin appears until it is switched on again.
